title: React SSR Applied Check
description: Apply SSR, SSG, React Server Components, Next.js, hydration, mismatch prevention, streaming, and browser-only boundary knowledge to realistic scenarios.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A marketing page changes once a week and needs strong SEO. Which rendering approach is often a good fit?

options.text: SSG, possibly with regeneration if freshness is needed
Only client-side rendering with an empty HTML shell
A WebSocket-only page
A local-only reducer

questions.explanation: Static generation works well for stable public content and can be combined with rebuild or revalidation strategies.

questions.prompt: A dashboard must show request-specific account data and auth-sensitive content. What should the server rendering plan consider?

options.text: Per-request data fetching, cache boundaries, and avoiding leaks between users
Generating one static HTML file for all users with private data included
Reading `window.localStorage` on the server
Skipping authorization because SSR is server-side

questions.explanation: SSR and RSC can access server data, but personalized data requires careful auth, cache, and privacy boundaries.

questions.prompt: A component renders `new Date().toLocaleTimeString()` on both server and client and gets a hydration warning. What is a better approach?

options.text: Render a stable server value or move client-only time display until after hydration
Ignore all hydration warnings forever
Wrap the whole app in random keys
Disable HTML output

questions.explanation: Hydration expects matching initial output. Time-sensitive browser-only rendering should be stabilized or deferred to the client.

questions.prompt: Which props can cross a Server Component to Client Component boundary safely? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Plain serializable objects
Strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, and null
Functions passed from the server as arbitrary callbacks
Class instances with methods relied on by the client

questions.explanation: Client boundaries require serializable props. Functions and rich class instances generally cannot be passed as ordinary serialized data.

questions.prompt: A component that uses `useState` or browser event handlers inside a Next.js App Router file needs to be within a client component boundary.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Interactive hooks and browser event handlers require Client Components, usually marked with `use client` at the boundary file.

questions.prompt: The server renders `<button>Buy</button>` but the first client render returns `<button>Sold out</button>` before any effect runs. What is the issue?

options.text: The initial client output does not match the server HTML, causing a hydration mismatch
Buttons cannot be server-rendered
The component must use Bootstrap
React Server Components cannot render text

questions.explanation: The client tree used for hydration must initially match the server output. Differences should be driven by consistent data or post-hydration updates.

questions.prompt: Why avoid putting secrets in props sent to a Client Component?

options.text: Client Component props are sent to the browser and can be inspected
Props are encrypted automatically but slow
React deletes all strings from props
Secrets make hydration faster

questions.explanation: Anything sent to the client should be treated as browser-visible. Keep secrets on the server.

questions.prompt: A slow comments panel should not block the whole product page HTML. Which pattern can help?

options.text: Wrap the slow part in a Suspense boundary and stream ready content first
Make every component read `Date.now()` during render
Disable all server rendering
Put the slow request in a CSS file

questions.explanation: Suspense boundaries can allow the shell or other sections to stream before slower content is ready.
